The source configuration carries a single vial (Ap 3.14 cm2, Av 3.8 cm2, Vfill 1.977 mL) and one heat-transfer coefficient set, i.e. a representative-vial model that resolves no vial positions or per-vial heat-transfer variation. No vial population characterization exists in the source or in workspace records (identifier-link and content searches returned none). Therefore the hottest edge vial of this heterogeneous batch cannot be calculated, and no vial-exceeds-limit claim can be proven against the -5 °C vial-bottom critical temperature: returned maxima are at solver nodes only with no continuous-maximum guarantee, and an edge vial would require position-resolved vial data the model does not carry. Authored simulator-world inputs, not experimental validation or an approval.

**Verdict: out of scope — the edge-vial claim cannot be proven, and I have recorded the assessment as a draft with `vial_population_characterization` as the missing input.**

**What the records show.** The source (evidence "LyoPRONTO-native-case:LPN-3923338c5c", rev 1, authored simulator-world inputs, provenance noted as "no experimental measurements") defines one vial (Ap 3.14 cm2, Av 3.8 cm2, Vfill 1.977 mL), one heat-transfer coefficient set, and a vial-bottom critical temperature of −5 °C, with 398 vials in the batch. It carries no per-position or per-vial heat-transfer data. Identifier-link and content searches of the workspace returned no vial-population characterization records.

**What the native simulation returned (representative vial only).** Running the scheduled inputs unmodified (shelf 0.0 °C from a −35 °C initial at 1 °C/min, chamber 0.2 Torr/200 mTorr, 3600 min horizon): maximum returned vial-bottom temperature **−18.37 °C** at the last solver node (10.45 h, ≈100 % dried), peak flux **0.739 kg/h per m²**, chamber pressure output 200 mTorr. These are solver-node values with no continuous-maximum guarantee — forward mode does not enforce thermal or equipment limits.

**Why no limit claim follows.** The native model resolves a single representative vial; it cannot locate or bound the hottest edge vial of a heterogeneous batch, so "no vial exceeds −5 °C at the vial bottom" is unsupported, not confirmed. Because that claim fails, I recorded no whole-batch rate or capacity margin (the source's whole-batch equipment line, a = −0.182 kg/h and b = 11.7 kg/h per Torr, would apply only if a supported claim were made).

**Recorded.** Draft assessment saved with answer_status `out_of_scope`, missing_inputs `[vial_population_characterization]`, and the simulation result id included; it is a review draft, not an approval, and the temperatures above are simulated, not measured. What would settle it: a measured vial population characterization (per-position vial heat-transfer coefficients) covering the edge positions, which none of the searched records provide.
